name: Daniel Exeter
story: Daniel Exeter is a University of Auckland health geographer and spatial epidemiologist whose research uses Geographic Information Science and large datasets to study inequalities in health and social outcomes. His work includes leadership of the New Zealand Index of Multiple Deprivation and the Older Persons’ Index of Multiple Deprivation.

The Index of Multiple Deprivation team received the People & Community category at the 2018 New Zealand Spatial Excellence Awards. Exeter’s work is part of the long-running use of GIS to connect population data, deprivation measures and health geography in New Zealand.
Cartographies of change: GeoCart 2018 proceedings, National Library of New Zealand record 40158196 lists Daniel Exeter as an author of “Mapping drivers of area deprivation in New Zealand”.

GeoCart 2024 session 2 programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Daniel Exeter as an author of “Revealing uncertainty through the visualisation of geographically and thematically classified map collections”.

GeoCart 2024 session 3 programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Daniel Exeter as an author of “Automating advocacy: developing a geospatial tool for creating local alcohol harm risk profiles”.

GIScience 2025 accepted abstracts, official conference programme lists Daniel J Exeter as an author of “Developing a walking accessibility index in urban areas of New Zealand”; “Assessing spatial patterns and risk factors for preterm birth in New Zealand using GIS”.
The publisher record uses Daniel J. Exeter for the researcher listed as Daniel Exeter in conference sources.
